name: French
description: Conversational French for travel and everyday life: cafés, trains, restaurants and small talk.

units.title: Salutations
units.note: `Ça va ?` and `Comment vas-tu ?` are for friends. `Comment allez-vous ?` is polite, or for a group. Say `Bonjour` during the day and `Bonsoir` in the evening; `Salut` means hi and bye among friends. Men write `enchanté`, women `enchantée`; they sound the same.

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.en: Hi, good morning.

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: Hello. How are you?

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.target: Ça va bien, merci. Et toi ?
dialogue.en: I'm fine, thanks. And you?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.target: Moi aussi, ça va. Comment tu t'appelles ?
dialogue.en: Fine too. What's your name?

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.en: My name is Camille. And you?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: My name is Léo. Nice to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.en: Nice to meet you. See you later!

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: Bye, see you later.

units.title: Tu viens d'où ?
units.note: The verb `être` (to be): `je suis, tu es, il/elle est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils/elles sont`. Unlike Spanish and Italian, French always keeps the pronoun. In everyday speech people often say `on` instead of `nous`: `on est touristes`.

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.en: Where are you from, Léo?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.target: Je suis de Chicago. Et toi ?
dialogue.en: I'm from Chicago. And you?

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.target: Je suis de Paris. Tu es étudiant ?
dialogue.en: I'm from Paris. Are you a student?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: No, I'm an engineer.

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.target: Et tes amis ? Ils sont d'ici ?
dialogue.en: And your friends? Are they from here?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: No, they're from London.

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.en: Are you all tourists?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: Yes, we're tourists.

answers: Ils ne sont pas de Londres.

units.title: Au café
units.note: `vouloir` (to want): `je veux, tu veux, il veut, nous voulons, vous voulez, ils veulent`. To order politely, say `je voudrais` (I'd like). Use `un` with masculine nouns and `une` with feminine ones. A plain `café` is an espresso; `un café crème` comes with milk.

dialogue.speaker: Serveur
dialogue.target: Bonjour, qu'est-ce que je vous sers ?
dialogue.en: Hello, what can I get you?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.target: Un café crème, s'il vous plaît.
dialogue.en: A coffee with milk, please.

dialogue.speaker: Serveur
dialogue.en: Anything else?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: A croissant, please.

dialogue.speaker: Serveur
dialogue.en: Very good.

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: How much do I owe you?

dialogue.speaker: Serveur
dialogue.en: That's three euros fifty.

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: Here you go. Thanks.

items.en: Do you want anything else? (one friend)

units.title: C'est où ?
units.note: `Où est ... ?` asks where something is; `Où sont ... ?` for several. `Il y a` means "there is" or "there are". Directions: `à droite` right, `à gauche` left, `tout droit` straight on.

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: Excuse me, where is the station?

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.target: C'est tout près. Tout droit, puis à droite.
dialogue.en: It's very close. Straight on, then right.

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: Is it far from here?

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.target: Non, c'est à cinq minutes à pied.
dialogue.en: No, it's five minutes on foot.

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.target: Il y a une pharmacie près d'ici ?
dialogue.en: Is there a pharmacy near here?

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.target: Oui, il y a une pharmacie à gauche, à côté de la banque.
dialogue.en: Yes, there's a pharmacy on the left, next to the bank.

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: Thank you very much.

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.en: You're welcome.

units.title: Au restaurant
units.note: `avoir` (to have): `j'ai, tu as, il a, nous avons, vous avez, ils ont`. A French menu runs `entrée` (starter), `plat` (main) and `dessert`. Tap water is free: ask for `une carafe d'eau`. Ask for the bill with `L'addition, s'il vous plaît`.

dialogue.speaker: Serveur
dialogue.en: Good evening. How many of you are there?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.target: Nous sommes deux. Vous avez une table ?
dialogue.en: There are two of us. Do you have a table?

dialogue.speaker: Serveur
dialogue.target: Oui, par ici. Voici la carte.
dialogue.en: Yes, this way. Here's the menu.

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: What do you recommend?

dialogue.speaker: Serveur
dialogue.en: The beef bourguignon is excellent.

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.target: D'accord. En entrée la soupe à l'oignon, et en plat le bœuf bourguignon.
dialogue.en: OK. Onion soup to start, and the beef bourguignon for the main.

dialogue.speaker: Serveur
dialogue.en: And to drink?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.target: Une carafe d'eau, s'il vous plaît.
dialogue.en: A jug of tap water, please.

units.title: Les transports
units.note: `aller` (to go): `je vais, tu vas, il va, nous allons, vous allez, ils vont`. Use `à` with cities (`à Lyon`); with places it joins the article: `à + le = au`, `à + les = aux`, but `à la` and `à l'` stay. Times: `à une heure`, `à dix heures`, `et demie` (half past), `et quart` (quarter past).

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.target: Bonjour, un billet pour Lyon, s'il vous plaît.
dialogue.en: Hello, a ticket to Lyon, please.

dialogue.speaker: Agent
dialogue.en: One way or return?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: Return, please.

dialogue.speaker: Agent
dialogue.en: That's eighty euros.

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.target: Le train part à quelle heure ?
dialogue.en: What time does the train leave?

dialogue.speaker: Agent
dialogue.target: Il part à dix heures et demie.
dialogue.en: It leaves at half past ten.

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: From which platform?

dialogue.speaker: Agent
dialogue.en: Platform five. Have a good trip.

Say the sentence again with the new word swapped in.

answers: Il part à dix heures et demie.
Il part à trois heures et quart.

units.title: Faire du shopping
units.note: `celui-ci` and `celle-ci` mean "this one". Most colours agree with the noun: `un pull noir`, `une robe noire`; `marron` and `orange` never change. Ask `C'est combien ?` or `Combien ça coûte ?`. `Je le prends` or `Je la prends` means "I'll take it".

dialogue.speaker: Vendeuse
dialogue.en: Hello, can I help you?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: Yes, I'm looking for a T-shirt.

dialogue.speaker: Vendeuse
dialogue.en: What size?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.target: Taille M. Vous l'avez en bleu ?
dialogue.en: Medium. Do you have it in blue?

dialogue.speaker: Vendeuse
dialogue.en: Yes, this one is blue.

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: How much is it?

dialogue.speaker: Vendeuse
dialogue.en: Fifteen euros.

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: Perfect, I'll take it.

units.title: On discute
units.note: `aimer` (to like, to love): `j'aime, tu aimes, il aime, nous aimons, vous aimez, ils aiment`. French keeps the article after it: `j'aime le café`. `adorer` means to love. Regular -er verbs like `parler` follow the same pattern.

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.en: What are you doing this weekend?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.target: Je vais au jardin du Luxembourg avec des amis.
dialogue.en: I'm going to the Luxembourg Gardens with some friends.

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.en: Great! Do you like Paris?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: Yes, I like it a lot.

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.en: And the food?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.en: I love it. I really like croissants.

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.en: Do you speak French at work?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.target: Un peu. Je parle presque toujours anglais.
dialogue.en: A little. I almost always speak English.

items.en: I'm going to the museum with some friends.
answers: Je vais au musée avec des amis.

units.title: Le travail
units.note: `travailler`: `je travaille, tu travailles, il travaille, nous travaillons, vous travaillez, ils travaillent`. `le lundi` means "on Mondays". `commencer` (to start) adds a cedilla to keep the soft sound: `nous commençons`.

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.target: Qu'est-ce que tu fais dans la vie ?
dialogue.en: What do you do for a living?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.target: Je suis ingénieur. Je travaille dans une entreprise de technologie.
dialogue.en: I'm an engineer. I work at a tech company.

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.en: Do you work in the office?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.target: Non, le lundi et le vendredi, je travaille de chez moi.
dialogue.en: No, on Mondays and Fridays I work from home.

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.target: Quelle chance ! Tu aimes ton travail ?
dialogue.en: Lucky you! Do you like your job?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.target: Oui, mais j'ai beaucoup de réunions.
dialogue.en: Yes, but I have a lot of meetings.

dialogue.speaker: Camille
dialogue.en: What time do you start?

dialogue.speaker: Léo
dialogue.target: Je commence à neuf heures et je finis à dix-huit heures.
dialogue.en: I start at nine and finish at six.
